meta.title: The Marsh Without a Grave
meta.tagline: Night falls, the marsh closes in, and something is still waiting for its name to be returned.

strings.ms.s01.title: The Edge
strings.ms.s01.body: You only wanted to walk for a while before nightfall. The path looked simple. But ahead of you, the marsh stretches farther than expected, dark, wet, silent. It is not night yet, but you already feel that you have gone too far.
strings.ms.s01.c3: Climb the mound for a better view
strings.ms.s02.title: Between the Reeds
strings.ms.s02.body: The path sinks between tall reeds. They brush softly against each other with no wind. The ground is soft. With each step, getting back seems a little less simple.
strings.ms.s02.c2: Look at what is shining in the reeds
strings.ms.s02.c3: Turn around to check the path
strings.ms.s03.title: The Still Water
strings.ms.s03.body: The water is so black it almost absorbs all the evening light. Nothing moves. Then a circle forms on the surface, as if something has just breathed beneath you.
strings.ms.s03.c1: Watch the edge of the reeds
strings.ms.s03.c3: Look for a drier patch of land
strings.ms.s04.title: The Mound
strings.ms.s04.body: From the small mound, you mostly see gray, water, tall grass, and paths that all look alike. You thought you would see the way out. All you see is a place where every path looks the same.
strings.ms.s04.c1: Go back down toward the flooded path
strings.ms.s05.title: The Old Sign
strings.ms.s05.body: An old sign leans on a rotting post. It must have pointed to an exit once. Now the arrow is almost eaten away by moisture. You can guess a direction, but you cannot trust it.
strings.ms.s05.c2: Move closer to the white shape
strings.ms.s06.title: The White Cloth
strings.ms.s06.body: A piece of white fabric is caught on the reeds. Too clean. Too visible. As if someone wanted to mark a passage or leave a sign. But for whom?
strings.ms.s06.c1: Look at the white shape in the distance
strings.ms.s07.title: Behind You
strings.ms.s07.body: You turn around. The path you just took already seems lower, more flooded, almost erased. You are not sure you can go back that way. The landscape already looks different.
strings.ms.s08.title: The Footbridge
strings.ms.s08.body: The old footbridge cracks under your weight. Black water moves slowly beneath it. You cannot see the bottom. You do not feel like you are crossing a simple marsh. You feel like you are entering another part of it.
strings.ms.s08.c3: Follow the marked post farther ahead
strings.ms.s09.title: The Islet
strings.ms.s09.body: The ground is a little less soft here. You can finally breathe without watching every step. But the silence is worse. On this small patch of land, you mostly feel very exposed.
strings.ms.s09.c3: Look at the map if you find shelter
strings.ms.s10.title: The Pond
strings.ms.s10.body: Bubbles slowly rise to the surface of the pond. One. Then two. Then nothing. You wait. Another rises closer. You step back without even realizing it.
strings.ms.s10.c3: Move closer to the small altar
strings.ms.s11.title: The Old Fence
strings.ms.s11.body: An old fence crosses the marsh before disappearing into the water. It once marked off something. On the other side, the grass is flattened, as if someone still passes through there.
strings.ms.s12.title: The Shape
strings.ms.s12.body: You can see it better now. A white shape, motionless, paler than the mist. It does not move like an animal. It does not look like a simple piece of cloth either. And yet, when you look again, it is already somewhere else.
strings.ms.s12.c3: Move closer to the small altar
strings.ms.s13.title: The Dead Willow
strings.ms.s13.body: The great willow leans very low over the black water. Its branches hang heavily. Beneath the tree, the earth is even darker. You smell damp cloth and cold soil.
strings.ms.s13.c3: Look at the small pile of stones
strings.ms.s14.title: The Boat
strings.ms.s14.body: The small boat is stuck against black roots. It is too damaged to use. Inside, there is nothing. Nothing except the strange feeling that it has not been empty for very long.
strings.ms.s15.title: The Cabin
strings.ms.s15.body: The cabin is still standing, but barely. The door is half open. The wood is damp and blackened. Right now, it almost seems welcoming, which makes you even more uneasy.
strings.ms.s15.c2: Leave the cabin and reach the post
strings.ms.s16.title: Inside
strings.ms.s16.body: A dirty table. A dull window. The smell of dry mud. Everything has been left in place, as if someone fled in a hurry and never came back.
strings.ms.s16.c1: Look at the map on the wall
strings.ms.s16.c3: Go out and follow the direction of the flooded hamlet
strings.ms.s17.title: The Map
strings.ms.s17.body: An old map of the marsh is pinned to the wall. Hand-drawn lines cross the water, the mounds, and several old places. The map does not give you a simple exit. It mostly shows you what truly matters here.
strings.ms.s17.c1: Look for another sign in the cabin
strings.ms.s17.c2: Leave through the passage of reeds
strings.ms.s18.title: The Hanging Objects
strings.ms.s18.body: Small bones, strings, and pieces of fabric hang from the ceiling. Nothing large. Nothing dramatic. Just enough to understand that this cabin was not only a shelter.
strings.ms.s18.c1: Go back toward the small altar
strings.ms.s19.title: The Flood Marker Post
strings.ms.s19.body: Lines are carved into a blackened post. Some have almost erased dates beside them. The highest mark is above your head. You look around and understand that the marsh can take everything back here.
strings.ms.s19.c2: Look at the pile of stones
strings.ms.s20.title: The Green Corridor
strings.ms.s20.body: The reeds tighten on both sides. The passage becomes almost straight, as if it had been forced open by hand. You no longer hear birds. Only the rubbing of the stalks against each other and your own breath.
strings.ms.s21.title: The Small Altar
strings.ms.s21.body: On a stump, someone left gray wax, an old broken bowl, and a wet red ribbon. This is not decoration. Someone came here to ask for something or calm something down.
strings.ms.s22.title: The Ribbon
strings.ms.s22.body: The red ribbon sticks slightly to your fingers. It is strangely heavy for a simple ribbon. It is only a piece of fabric, but you feel like you are taking something that should never have left this place.
strings.ms.s22.c1: Go toward the pile of stones
strings.ms.s22.c2: Follow the path toward the hamlet
strings.ms.s23.title: The Boards
strings.ms.s23.body: The poorly aligned boards lead you away from the deep water. Each step forces you to watch where you put your feet. It is slow, but better than walking blindly through the mud.
strings.ms.s23.c3: Look for the well in the square
strings.ms.s24.title: The Small Cairn
strings.ms.s24.body: The pile of stones is too neat to be natural. Someone placed these stones here, one by one. Between two of them, you see a small white shard that looks like a piece of bone. You would rather not touch it.
strings.ms.s25.title: The Flooded Hamlet
strings.ms.s25.body: The marsh opens onto a few low houses, half taken by water. It is not a whole village. Just enough to make you believe that life once existed here. Just enough to understand that it ended badly.
strings.ms.s25.c2: Go toward the old post office
strings.ms.s26.title: The Square
strings.ms.s26.body: The well at the center seems even darker than the rest of the marsh. The stones around it are smooth and wet. You look at the houses, the doors, the dirty windows. Nothing moves. Nothing lives. And yet, you clearly feel a presence.
strings.ms.s26.c2: Go toward the old post office
strings.ms.s27.title: The Closed Building
strings.ms.s27.body: The low building has almost no windows. The opaque panes reveal nothing. The door will not open. The place looks like it has been closed for a long time, but you do not believe it is empty.
strings.ms.s27.c1: Go toward the old post office
strings.ms.s28.title: The Old Post Office
strings.ms.s28.body: The small post office seems to have been emptied by water and then forgotten. A rusty mailbox still hangs near the door. It looks as if the messages stayed trapped here.
strings.ms.s28.c2: Look at the letters on the floor
strings.ms.s29.title: The Counter
strings.ms.s29.body: Inside, the counter still stands. Damp, stuck-together bags rest in one corner. Everything is swollen with water. If someone kept records here, they did not age well.
strings.ms.s29.c3: Leave the post office and return to the square
strings.ms.s30.title: The Damp Letters
strings.ms.s30.body: Letters stuck to the floor still carry traces of ink. The names are almost erased. Some envelopes are empty. Others seem never to have been opened. As if the messages stayed trapped here with the dead.
strings.ms.s31.title: The Stable
strings.ms.s31.body: The stalls are empty. The straw is black and wet. You hear water dripping somewhere, very slowly. The place gives no answer, but it adds weight to the silence.
strings.ms.s32.title: The Chapel
strings.ms.s32.body: The small chapel still stands at the end of a black, soft stretch of ground. Its front is plain. Its door seems lighter than the doors of the other buildings. As if this place has always been waiting for someone to enter.
strings.ms.s33.title: The Nave
strings.ms.s33.body: The inside is poor and cold. A few twisted benches. A simple altar. A damp smell of stone and old fabric. But you quickly notice a small object near the altar, left in plain sight.
strings.ms.s33.c2: Read the names carved into the wall
strings.ms.s34.title: The Side Room
strings.ms.s34.body: The small adjoining room contains an open cabinet, moldy linen, and a few broken ceremonial objects. Then you see the bell, set apart as if someone wanted it to remain easy to find.
strings.ms.s34.c2: Read the names carved into the wall
strings.ms.s35.title: The Small Bell
strings.ms.s35.body: The bell fits in one hand. Its metal is cold. You do not try to ring it here. You already feel that it is not meant for just any place.
strings.ms.s36.title: The Carved Names
strings.ms.s36.body: Names have been carved by hand into a wall. Some are clear. Others have been scratched out or left unfinished. Here, people tried to keep a trace of those who could not rest anywhere else.
strings.ms.s37.title: The Flooded Cemetery
strings.ms.s37.body: Behind the chapel, gravestones lean in the shallow water. Some seem empty. Others still carry names eaten by moss. The place is small, but it is enough to understand that not everyone was given a grave.
strings.ms.s38.title: The Open Grave
strings.ms.s38.body: The grave has been open for a long time. The wood is broken, the earth is cold, and the pit no longer tells anything simple. You do not see a body. You mostly see the absence of what should have been resting here.
strings.ms.s38.c3: Climb up to see the marsh from above
strings.ms.s39.title: The Bone Path
strings.ms.s39.body: Between the grass and the mud, bleached fragments almost form a small path. You could say they are stones. But no. You know very well they are not stones.
strings.ms.s40.title: The Platform
strings.ms.s40.body: The old wooden structure still holds. From up there, you should be able to see the exit. Instead, you see the problem more clearly. Several paths loop back on themselves. The marsh always sends you back toward its center.
strings.ms.s40.c2: Read the plan carved into the wood
strings.ms.s40.c3: Follow the line of stones below
strings.ms.s41.title: The Marsh from Above
strings.ms.s41.body: From the height, you spot the cabin, the hamlet, the chapel, and the pump house. Farther away, you also make out a central mound you had not seen before. This place is not random. Everything seems arranged around a center.
strings.ms.s42.title: The Carved Plan
strings.ms.s42.body: Someone carved a plan into the wood with a blade. Lines connect the old places of the marsh. Some converge toward the central mound. Others stop near a technical installation. Here, people organized the dead at the same time as the water.
strings.ms.s43.title: The Stones in the Water
strings.ms.s43.body: A line of stones rises out of the black water and then sinks back into it. You have to move slowly so you do not slip. They seem to lead in several possible directions, depending on where you leave the line.
strings.ms.s44.title: The Pump House
strings.ms.s44.body: The metal building seems out of place in the middle of this old marsh. And yet, it makes sense here. Someone wanted to hold back, move, and control the water. Maybe also to hide what it once covered.
strings.ms.s45.title: The Pumps
strings.ms.s45.body: The large rusty engine sleeps beneath a layer of moisture. Water stagnates on the floor. Pipes run in several directions, like a network that connected the whole marsh. The place smells of old effort and even older failure.
strings.ms.s45.c3: Look for the sluice behind it
strings.ms.s46.title: The Valves
strings.ms.s46.body: Valves, chains, and levers eaten by rust surround the room. You then understand that the water was once guided, held back, then released here. The marsh was not always free.
strings.ms.s47.title: The Small Office
strings.ms.s47.body: The office is narrow. A table, a shelf, papers stuck together. This must be where people recorded floods, repairs, and closures. Maybe also things that do not belong in a real public record.
strings.ms.s47.c2: Take the damp page sticking out
strings.ms.s47.c3: Go out toward the passage behind
strings.ms.s48.title: The Registers
strings.ms.s48.body: The old registers are covered in dry mud. Most lines are unreadable. But some pages mention impossible burials, lost ground, and bodies moved by the water. You read just enough to understand the heart of the legend.
strings.ms.s48.c1: Take the page where a name is missing
strings.ms.s49.title: The Missing Name
strings.ms.s49.body: The page is damp, but still readable. One entire line waits for a name that was never filled in. Everything else was recorded. Date. Place. State of the body. Then a blank. As if someone refused to complete one specific person’s rest.
strings.ms.s49.c1: Keep the page and move on
strings.ms.s49.c2: Follow the trail toward the large stone
strings.ms.s50.title: Behind the Pumps
strings.ms.s50.body: Behind the building, a narrow metal passage leads to a small sluice and a path farther into the mist. It is less ancient than the rest, but just as sinister. As if someone wanted to work quickly on a very old problem.
strings.ms.s50.c3: Follow the white shapes in the water
strings.ms.s51.title: The Sluice
strings.ms.s51.body: The water still pushes against the worn boards. Not enough to make noise. Just enough to remind you that it is waiting for the slightest weakness. You wonder what people tried to keep inside or outside.
strings.ms.s52.title: The Secret Path
strings.ms.s52.body: The long board path disappears into the mist, then returns, very thin, very straight. You cannot see what it passes over. You would rather not know. Still, it leads toward something central.
strings.ms.s53.title: The White Circle
strings.ms.s53.body: Several white shapes are motionless in the water, arranged in a circle. They do not look at you. They do nothing. That is worse. You understand that they are waiting for a gesture, a sound, a name, something that has not yet come.
strings.ms.s54.title: The Large Stone
strings.ms.s54.body: The standing stone bears traces of very old offerings. Wax. Earth. Thread. Scratches. People came here to ask forgiveness or calm the marsh. You immediately feel that this place is connected to the central mound.
strings.ms.s54.c1: Read the names carved on it
strings.ms.s54.c3: Follow the chain in the water
strings.ms.s55.title: The Names in the Stone
strings.ms.s55.body: The stone carries incomplete, worn, repeated names. Some come back to you because you have already seen them carved elsewhere. The marsh tried to preserve what the earth could not keep.
strings.ms.s56.title: The Hollow Oak
strings.ms.s56.body: The oak is old, hollow, and almost black. Its inside is empty, but not clean. Someone has hidden things in there before. You find nothing, except the certainty that this marsh was used for more than separating two areas.
strings.ms.s57.title: The Post
strings.ms.s57.body: The old mooring post has no boat left. Only deep marks left by ropes or chains. Something was transported here. Or someone. And it happened often.
strings.ms.s57.c1: Follow the chain in the water
strings.ms.s58.title: The Chain
strings.ms.s58.body: The dark chain disappears under the black water and comes back out farther away, almost like a guide. You follow it with your eyes and see that it goes toward the central mound. There is no doubt anymore. Everything leads there.
strings.ms.s59.title: The Thin Passage
strings.ms.s59.body: You move between water that is too dark and mud that could take your leg in a second. Here, there is no room for hesitation. Only for keeping your balance and continuing.
strings.ms.s60.title: The Small Bank
strings.ms.s60.body: The ground is finally a little stable. Ahead of you, the central mound rises over the rest of the marsh like a badly closed grave. Farther on, there is also a pale glow that could almost pass for an exit.
strings.ms.s60.c3: Follow the glow of the exit
strings.ms.s61.title: The Central Mound
strings.ms.s61.body: The wind is colder here. Low crosses, stones, and ancient marks surround the mound. You understand before even finding the entrance that this place is the heart of the marsh.
strings.ms.s61.c2: Follow an opening on the side of the mound
strings.ms.s61.c3: Reach the large cairn farther away
strings.ms.s62.title: The Stone Door
strings.ms.s62.body: An old stone door is set into the mound. It is not truly locked. It is heavy, but it gives way. The air that comes out is cold, damp, and older than everything you have crossed so far.
strings.ms.s63.title: The Low Corridor
strings.ms.s63.body: The passage is so low you almost have to bend in half. Roots cross through the earthen ceiling. Water drips slowly. Here, the marsh no longer seems only above you. It also seems around you, inside the walls themselves.
strings.ms.s64.title: The Stretchers
strings.ms.s64.body: Old empty stretchers are lined up in an underground room. Everything is simple, sad, practical. Bodies were brought here. Maybe prepared here. Then something stopped in the middle of the work.
strings.ms.s65.title: The Plaques
strings.ms.s65.body: The wall carries dull plaques, sometimes without dates, sometimes without full names. Many are incomplete. So the problem was not one forgotten dead person. The problem was larger. Older.
strings.ms.s66.title: The Basin
strings.ms.s66.body: The small stone basin is black, but not deep. You can almost make out the bottom. Almost. Mostly, you see the trembling reflection of your face, then another one behind you. You turn around. No one is there.
strings.ms.s67.title: The Breath
strings.ms.s67.body: The round opening in the floor lets out a cold breath. Not a normal draft. It almost sounds like a breath trying to form a word, if you stay too long listening to it. You do not like what it is trying to say.
strings.ms.s67.c3: Step back toward the white faces
strings.ms.s68.title: The Rising Water
strings.ms.s68.body: Water slowly spreads between the stones. The place is not filling quickly. It is closing in on the time you have left. Soon you will have to choose between fleeing and understanding.
strings.ms.s68.c2: Follow the glow in the distance
strings.ms.s68.c3: Go out toward the pale reeds
strings.ms.s69.title: The Separation
strings.ms.s69.body: The passage splits into two damp branches. One seems more direct. The other seems to lead back outside. The marsh never gives you a truly simple choice. Only choices that cost something.
strings.ms.s69.c2: Go out toward the pale reeds
strings.ms.s70.title: The Glow
strings.ms.s70.body: A thin bright line appears in the distance. It could almost be an exit. Not quite a real exit. Just enough to bring hope back.
strings.ms.s71.title: The Pale Reeds
strings.ms.s71.body: Some reeds are paler than the others, almost marked. They draw a discreet passage. Without your attention, you would have taken it for a simple trick of the light.
strings.ms.s71.c2: Follow the red traces if you can
strings.ms.s72.title: The Faces
strings.ms.s72.body: In the thick mist, white faces barely appear. Not whole faces. Just enough features to understand that they still want to be recognized. Here, forgetting has a shape.
strings.ms.s72.c2: Listen to the silence around you
strings.ms.s73.title: The Large Cairn
strings.ms.s73.body: The large cairn of black stones rises over calm water. Unlike the small pile you saw earlier, this one is clearly central. It is not a single grave. It is a gathering point.
strings.ms.s73.c3: Read the stones at the foot of the cairn
strings.ms.s74.title: The Missing Sound
strings.ms.s74.body: Around the cairn, the air feels suspended. You have the impression that one precise sound should exist here. You look at the stone, the water, and the mist. Everything remains still, as if held in place.
strings.ms.s74.c3: Follow the path that leads away
strings.ms.s75.title: The Slab
strings.ms.s75.body: Beneath the half-open slab, there is no body. Only a black void, a few stones, and proof that someone tried to close something without succeeding. The marsh was not soothed. It was only covered.
strings.ms.s75.c3: Follow the path that leads away
strings.ms.s76.title: The Bell at the Cairn
strings.ms.s76.body: The sound of the bell is small, but it travels through everything. The water shivers. The white shapes do not move, then turn slightly. You feel that you have finally made a gesture this place understands.
strings.ms.s76.c3: Try the exit while the place is listening
strings.ms.s77.title: The Path That Leads Away
strings.ms.s77.body: Another path seems to lead back toward the heart of the marsh. It is tempting to believe there is another answer somewhere else. But you mostly feel that this path will only pull you even deeper into the marsh if you trust it too much.
strings.ms.s77.c1: Reach the marks in the reeds
strings.ms.s77.c2: Observe the water that is too clear
strings.ms.s78.title: The Red Marks
strings.ms.s78.body: In some reeds, you finally make out a discreet red presence. Without the ribbon you took earlier, you might not have noticed it. The marsh does not give you a road. It only gives you a thread.
strings.ms.s78.c2: Force your way through the last path
strings.ms.s79.title: The Mirror Water
strings.ms.s79.body: A sheet of calm water reflects a sky far too bright to be real. Looking closer, you think you see something else under the surface. A written line. A name almost returned. Not complete yet, but close.
strings.ms.s79.c1: Listen to what the marsh shows
strings.ms.s80.title: The Almost Firm Ground
strings.ms.s80.body: The earth grows harder beneath your feet. You could almost believe the exit is there. Almost. But the marsh is behind you, still present, still attentive. Leaving now or looking back one more time could change everything.
strings.ms.s81.title: The Final Threshold
strings.ms.s81.body: Here, everything seems to meet. The cairn. The mist. The mound. The old gestures. The marsh does not only want to lose you. Everything gives the impression that something has been missing from this place for all these years.
strings.ms.s81.c3: Give up and let the marsh decide
strings.ms.s82.title: The Returned Name
strings.ms.s82.body: The missing name does not appear all at once. It returns piece by piece, as if the place is finally allowing it to come back. You understand that the true way out is not only to leave. It is also to give this place back what was refused to it.
strings.ms.s82.c1: Carry the name to the final choice
strings.ms.s83.title: The Last Path
strings.ms.s83.body: The narrow path passes between the black stone and the firmer ground. Everything still seems possible, but not for long. You no longer feel only fear. You also feel the weight of what you might leave behind if you run too quickly.
strings.ms.s84.title: The Final Choice
strings.ms.s84.body: You have reached the point where everything is decided. Leave. Turn around. Or finally finish what was left incomplete here. The marsh is no longer only a trap. It has become a question. And it is waiting for your answer.
strings.ms.s84.c3: Return the name to the cairn and close the wound
strings.ms.good_end.title: ENDING — You Get Out
strings.ms.good_end.body: You walk to firm ground without looking back even once. At dawn, the marsh is behind you. You can finally breathe. You have not understood everything. But you are alive, and that is enough for today.
strings.ms.bad_end.title: ENDING — One More Shape
strings.ms.bad_end.body: You look back one time too many. The mist approaches without a sound. The white shapes no longer seem far away. When daylight returns, the marsh keeps one more silhouette. And no one outside will ever know your name.
strings.ms.secret_end.title: SECRET ENDING — Rest Returned
strings.ms.secret_end.body: You ring the bell, follow the red thread, and finally return the missing name to the cairn. The marsh changes at once. Not all at once, not like a miracle. Just enough to understand that the wound has closed. The white shapes stop waiting. For the first time, this place knows rest.
strings.ms.h.s05.soft: The old sign may not be reliable. Look instead for what seems to have been left on purpose.
strings.ms.h.s05.strong: The white fabric and the big tree are more useful than the sign for moving forward.
strings.ms.h.s15.soft: The cabin does not give you the exit, but it helps you understand the marsh.
strings.ms.h.s15.strong: Enter the cabin. The map and the signs inside truly matter.
strings.ms.h.s17.soft: The map does not give a simple path. It mostly shows the places that matter.
strings.ms.h.s17.strong: Remember the central mound and the pump house. Everything eventually leads there.
strings.ms.h.s21.soft: The small altar is not decorative. It holds a useful object.
strings.ms.h.s21.strong: Take the red ribbon. It will be useful for the true path later.
strings.ms.h.s25.soft: The flooded hamlet contains several pieces of the answer.
strings.ms.h.s25.strong: The post office, the chapel, and the cemetery are the most useful areas for progress.
strings.ms.h.s32.soft: The chapel is not the exit. It is a passage toward something deeper.
strings.ms.h.s32.strong: Enter the chapel and look for the small bell.
strings.ms.h.s33.soft: An object left alone near the altar is never there by chance.
strings.ms.h.s33.strong: Take the bell. It is needed for the secret ending.
strings.ms.h.s44.soft: The old technical installation is not unrelated. It explains how the place was managed.
strings.ms.h.s44.strong: Search the pumps, then the office, to find what the marsh is truly missing.
strings.ms.h.s47.soft: The papers in the office matter more than the old machines.
strings.ms.h.s47.strong: Take the damp page with the missing name. It is essential for the secret ending.
strings.ms.h.s54.soft: The large stone prepares the way for the large cairn.
strings.ms.h.s54.strong: Then go to the central mound and the large cairn. That is the right path forward.
strings.ms.h.s61.soft: The mound is the heart of the marsh. You cannot finish without returning to it.
strings.ms.h.s61.strong: Enter through the stone door or reach the large cairn for the final phase.
strings.ms.h.s74.soft: Around the cairn, everything seems to be waiting for one precise gesture.
strings.ms.h.s74.strong: If you have the bell, ring it here.
strings.ms.h.s78.soft: The red traces are only clear if you took the right object earlier.
strings.ms.h.s78.strong: The red ribbon helps you read the true path toward the secret ending.
strings.ms.h.s82.soft: The missing name is not just a story detail. It is needed to complete the story properly.
strings.ms.h.s82.strong: Secret ending: you need the red ribbon, the bell, and the page with the missing name.
strings.ms.h.s84.soft: The final choice mostly depends on what you have understood and kept with you.
strings.ms.h.s84.strong: Good ending: leave. Bad ending: give in or look back at the wrong moment. Secret ending: return the name to the cairn with the three items.
